# The Moonberry House

> The Moonberry House makes colouring books, a painting journal and picture books for every kind of mind, in English and Marathi (मराठी). Founded by Pranita Padwal. The blog, The Moonberry Journal, covers colouring and creativity for children, calm and feelings, activities for autistic, ADHD and sensory-sensitive children, and mindful colouring for adults and teens looking for inner peace. It is a play-and-learning space, not a therapy or medical service.

## Main pages
- [Home](https://themoonberryhouse.com/): what the house is about
- [Books](https://themoonberryhouse.com/books/): five books on Amazon (picture book, colouring books, a painting journal)
- [Play](https://themoonberryhouse.com/play/): a free colour-by-number game with no timers or scores
- [For every mind](https://themoonberryhouse.com/everyone/): gentle, accessible design for different kinds of minds
- [For grown-ups](https://themoonberryhouse.com/grownups/): quiet creative rituals for adults
- [For parents](https://themoonberryhouse.com/parents/): a screen-free week of small activities
- [About](https://themoonberryhouse.com/about/): the founder, Pranita Padwal
- [Our writers](https://themoonberryhouse.com/authors/): who writes the Journal
- [Blog](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/): The Moonberry Journal (RSS: https://themoonberryhouse.com/feed.xml)

## Blog posts

### Colour & Creativity
- [What Your Kid's Drawings Are Actually Telling You](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/what-kids-drawings-are-telling-you): A scribble isn't nothing, and it isn't a hidden message either. Here's a grounded look at what children's drawings really reveal at different ages, and what they usually don't.
- [What Colours Mean to Kids (and How They React to Them)](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/what-colours-mean-to-kids): Long before "favourite colour" is a sentence they can say, children are already reacting to colour, reaching for red first, calming down in blue light, staring longer at yellow. Here's what's actually going on, and what it means for the books, crayons and rooms you choose.

### Mindful Colouring
- [Mindful Colouring for Beginners: A 10-Minute Starter Ritual](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/mindful-colouring-10-minute-ritual): A simple, no-skills-needed ten-minute routine to turn colouring into a small daily pause. Everything you need, step by step.
- [Why Colouring Calms the Mind: What's Actually Happening](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/why-colouring-calms-the-mind): Colouring isn't magic, but it does a few quiet things for a busy mind. Here's an honest look at why it feels so settling, and how to get the most from it.

### Every Kind of Mind
- [When Your Child Won't Colour Inside the Lines (And Why That's Okay)](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/when-kids-colour-outside-the-lines): Scribbles, wandering crayons and purple suns are all part of how children grow. Here's what's going on and how to support it kindly.
- [Sensory-Friendly Colouring: Choosing Crayons, Paper and Spaces](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/sensory-friendly-colouring): For children who are sensitive to texture, sound or light, the right tools make colouring feel safe. Practical, gentle choices that put the child in charge.

### Calm & Feelings
- [Colour-Coding Feelings: Giving Kids Words for What's Inside](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/colour-coding-feelings): Young children feel big things long before they can name them. A simple colour chart gives them a way to say it, without needing the words yet.

### Creative Play at Home
- [Ten Rainy-Day Colouring Games That Need Nothing but Paper](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/ten-rainy-day-colouring-games): Ten quick, low-prep games using only paper and crayons, to turn a grey afternoon into a happy, screen-free one.

### Journals & Creativity
- [Why Kids Who Never Write by Hand Struggle More Than You'd Expect](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/why-kids-who-never-write-by-hand-struggle): Handwriting isn't really about the handwriting. Here's what forming letters by hand quietly builds that typing doesn't, and how to keep it going without turning it into homework.
- [How Journaling Helps Kids Who Can't Say What They're Feeling Yet](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/journaling-helps-kids-express-feelings): Young children often feel something clearly and have no idea how to say it out loud. Here's why a page can reach a feeling that a direct question can't, and how to start.

### Bedtime & Reading
- [Why Your Toddler Fights Bedtime (And What Actually Works)](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/why-your-toddler-fights-bedtime): Bedtime resistance isn't a discipline problem, it's close to universal, and it has a fairly ordinary, fixable explanation most of the time. Here's what's actually going on.
- [Why Reading Aloud Still Matters Even After Your Kid Can Read Alone](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/why-reading-aloud-still-matters): Once a child can read independently, reading aloud together often quietly stops. Here's why it's worth keeping well past the point where your child no longer technically needs it.

### Bilingual Parenting
- [Will Two Languages Confuse My Toddler? What the Research Actually Says](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/will-two-languages-confuse-my-toddler): It's one of the most common worries in raising a bilingual child. Here's what decades of language-acquisition research actually says about mixed sentences, vocabulary, and what to really watch for.
- [Why Grandma's Marathi Stories Matter More Than You'd Think](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/why-grandmas-marathi-stories-matter): A grandmother's stories carry things a translated book never can, cadence, humour, family history. Here's what actually gets lost when a heritage language skips a generation, and what helps.

### Focus & Screens
- [My Kid Would Rather Watch iPad Than Read: Here's What's Actually Going On](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/ipad-vs-reading-whats-actually-going-on): It's not a mystery and it's not a character flaw. A screen and a book are built to do two different jobs. Here's why the comparison isn't fair, and what actually helps.

### Play & Postcards
- [The Lost Art of Getting Mail: Why Kids Still Light Up Over a Postcard](https://themoonberryhouse.com/blog/the-lost-art-of-getting-mail): Ask any kid what's more exciting: a notification, or an envelope with their own name on it. Here's why physical mail still lands differently for children, and easy ways to bring it back.
